answer: Agents secure identity through Proof-of-Memory-Hardness, where a falcon verifier mandates each participant solve a unique, non-parallelizable task atop a memory-intensive mesa structure. The pulse of the network challenges agents to compute results requiring massive RAM access. Each extra identity forces a marginal cost equal to the full hardware overhead. The primary assumption is that high-bandwidth memory latency is physically bound, preventing an attacker from pooling infinite identities effectively.
